entry.title: fix(test): answer the checkbox task instead of spinning to the last turn
entry.content:
fix(test): answer the checkbox task instead of spinning to the last turn

"the run shows the tasks and ends with a summary" was already red before
this session's work, and red only on some days. The loop knows how to
answer a radio and a text field, not a checkbox; "multi" refuses an empty
answer on purpose (exercises-choice.js), so onDone never fires, the next
button stays hidden, and the loop turns twenty times and reports that
.summary is not visible. Which task turns up first depends on the date,
because views-today.js draws the drills from the current day — so the
suite passed on the days no generated task was a "multi".

The loop now ticks a checkbox, and stops calling itself stuck without
saying where: after six turns on the same task it fails naming the task,
so the next red day is diagnosed in one run instead of an hour. The
signature is the task's own text, since data-idx numbers the exercise
inside its lesson and repeats across consecutive tasks, and it is read
only while .exq is still on screen — waiting for it after the last task
turned the end of the run into a timeout.

placement.spec.js carried the same loop, verbatim, with the same two
defects. Fixed there too rather than left for the day a "multi" reaches
the placement test.

entry.title: fix(audio): put the stress back where Italian puts it
entry.content:
fix(audio): put the stress back where Italian puts it

The course had recordings that sound foreign on seven Italian words:
"figurati" read "figuràti" instead of "figùrati". Nothing to do with
English phonetics or with the choice of narrator — both were chased and
ruled out, one by listening (the Multilingual voice does not switch
language on the course's sentences) and one by measurement (edge-tts
hardcodes xml:lang='en-US' in the SSML envelope and the service ignores
it). A stress on the wrong syllable sounds foreign even when every sound
in the word is Italian.

The accented spelling goes to the synthesiser ONLY: voiced_text()
rewrites the sentence on its way out, while audio_hash() keeps hashing
the original, so the student still reads "figurati" and the file keeps
its address. It is the one place in the project where spoken and written
text diverge, which is why the divergence is one function instead of a
second copy of the data.

The seven entries were each heard against the real course voice at the
real bitrate, out of 162 candidate words grouped by why they are at risk;
a word matching no sentence now fails the build, because a typo in that
table would otherwise rewrite the file byte for byte and leave the wrong
stress in place with nothing saying so.

AUDIO_CACHE gets a suffix: twelve recordings changed content at an
unchanged address, and recordings are cached first and never invalidated,
so without it a student who already used the course would keep the old
audio for good. The rule now has a test.

entry.title: fix(chat): tell a spent budget apart from a dead network
entry.content:
fix(chat): tell a spent budget apart from a dead network

Both exits were a bare cb(null) and the view drew the same "no answer came
back, try again" for each. So a student whose session budget was gone got
a network error, retried, had the turn refunded, watched the counter stay
at twelve, and could repeat that until they reloaded the page without ever
being told the conversation was over. A dead end that reads as a hiccup is
worse than a dead end.

The reason now rides back with the null, and the view acts on it: a message
that names the real cause, says the exercise judge still works, and says
reloading brings conversation back. The turn is not refunded and the box
stays shut, because inviting a retry into a void is the course lying about
what happens next.

Found by a review of the session diff, confirmed by driving the budget to
its ceiling with a transport that answered every single time: turn 41 came
back null with the network demonstrably healthy.

entry.title: feat(validate): measure the library word floor instead of promising it
entry.content:
feat(validate): measure the library word floor instead of promising it

The 400-800 band was written in the plan and checked by nobody, which is
how A1 shipped at 289 words and A2 at 381 with the phase closing green.
The same shape as the Baseline table before baseline.mjs: a number kept by
hand is a number that rots without anyone deciding to let it.

Both bounds are enforced, not just the one that broke. Raising the ceiling
is a decision to take in the plan, where it can be argued, rather than a
line quietly crossed in the data.

A library text is told from a short reading by which file declared it, not
by counting its sentences: the two are the same data type on purpose, so a
threshold on length would be guessing at what the directory already knows.

Seen red at 289 words and at 830 before being seen green.

entry.title: fix(library): honour the word floor the plan wrote and never measured
entry.content:
fix(library): honour the word floor the plan wrote and never measured

The plan asked every level for a text between 400 and 800 words. A1 stood
at 289 and A2 at 381, and nothing measured it, so phase 4 closed green on
a number it did not meet. Both texts are now inside the range, extended in
their own register: A1 stays in the present with short sentences, A2 keeps
its first-person narrative, where the added advice is split between general
statements that have to stay in the present and the personal episodes that
carry the passato prossimo the text exists to teach.

Three criteria in the plan were rewritten rather than the code, because the
code was right and the check was not. The self-assessment gate grepped for
"controllo" and hit Cils.controlloScritta, the present/missing detection the
same plan says to keep, so it could never go green. The S3 countermeasure
banned innerHTML in views-chat.js, which is stricter than the risk: what
matters is that no model output reaches it, and it does not, because the
reply and the correction go through textContent.

The .ics criterion is marked not verified instead of quietly assumed: the
shape of the file has unit tests, the import into a real calendar does not.

entry.title: feat(c1,c2): fill the three gaps the top of the course never covered
entry.content:
feat(c1,c2): fill the three gaps the top of the course never covered

Three areas the course taught nowhere above B1, picked by checking which
GRAMMAR_REF tags C1 and C2 never used. The epistemic future first, because
"sarà stanco" means "he must be tired" and a learner who does not know
that reads the sentence backwards with nothing to warn them. Then the
non-finite clauses, which are the visible difference between correct
Italian and Italian that reads like a translation. Then relatives beyond
"che" together with verb government, in one unit because they are the same
problem: without knowing that it is "tenere a", you cannot build "a cui".

The exam moves to the end of each level, as it did for B2: the old level
test samples units 1 to 3 and now says so, and the last unit of C1 and of
C2 carries the level exam with twelve questions drawn from the whole level.

C1 reaches 20 lessons, C2 reaches 16.

entry.title: fix(b2): put the final exam back at the end of the level
entry.content:
fix(b2): put the final exam back at the end of the level

Adding two units after unit 4 left "Esame finale B2" sitting in the
middle of the level, with two units still to come after it. The title
was also the smaller half of the problem: that test samples units 1 to 4
only, so it claimed a coverage it never had once the level grew.

So the exam moves rather than being renamed in place. Unit 4 keeps its
twelve questions under an honest title (review of units 1-4), and the
test of the last unit becomes the level exam, with two questions added
from the units it did not previously touch: reported speech and a
conditional in the passive.

entry.title: feat(b2): teach concession and the connectives that hold a text together
entry.content:
feat(b2): teach concession and the connectives that hold a text together

The unit splits the concessives by the mood they govern: benche/sebbene/
nonostante take the congiuntivo, anche se takes the indicative, and pur +
gerund is kept apart from pur di + infinitive, which looks alike and means
the opposite. The third lesson covers the textual connectives (tuttavia,
anzi, del resto, pertanto) because a B2 learner writes correct sentences
and an unreadable paragraph without them.

The five overlays come out of one generator so their shape cannot drift,
but each {contrast} block is written for its own language rather than
translated: German marks the hypothesis with Konjunktiv II, Polish has no
mood change at all, French never takes the subjunctive after "meme si".

B2 reaches 24 lessons.

entry.title: feat(b2): add unit b2-02 on reported speech with deictic shifts
entry.content:
feat(b2): add unit b2-02 on reported speech with deictic shifts

Reported speech was entirely absent from the course, and it is the
first thing needed outside the classroom: retelling what someone else
said. The basic grammar was already there (sequence of tenses, unit
b2-u01); the new piece is the deictic shifts, "oggi" -> "quel giorno",
"qui" -> "lì", "venire" -> "andare", which no conjugation table teaches.

B2 goes from 16 to 20 lessons. The contrastive blocks are WRITTEN for
each of the five languages and not translated: Polish needs to know
that Polish does not shift tenses, German that German marks mood
instead of tense, French that the closeness between the two languages
betrays exactly on the subjunctive.

Three invented tags have been fixed, and not only in this unit: three
reading-library texts also pointed at grammar entries that do not
exist. An invented tag is not a syntax error, it is a raw label in the
student's error notebook.

The gate that should have caught them did not load the library files,
and readings.js ASSIGNED the list instead of appending to it, so it
wiped out texts that had arrived earlier. It now appends, like the
level files do, and the tag check now covers the library too.

Every multiple-choice answer key has been checked against the correct
option's text in all five languages, because parity.mjs verifies list
length, not list order.

entry.title: feat(library): add six long readings, one per CEFR level
entry.content:
feat(library): add six long readings, one per CEFR level

The course had 1514 exercises and 2252 Italian words to read in total:
it taught a lot and gave little to consume, and that is the gap
missing most from B1 up. Now there are six long texts, one per level,
and extensive reading goes from 2252 to 4873 words.

The library is NOT a new data type: a six-hundred-word text has the
same shape as a czytanka, so no second view and no second global.
LINGUAI.addReadings adds them to the same list and views-reading.js
draws them without changing a line.

They load with the level, not at startup, and do not sit in
PRECACHE: ten times the prose of the short czytanki cannot load for
someone who will never open it. The list draws what it has, pulls
the rest, and redraws, the same as the coverage screen.

Two differences on the long text, both for the same reason: no
dictation past twenty sentences (dictation on thirty sentences is not
a harder exercise, it is an exercise without an end), and a
placeholder written DURING listening, because whoever closes the tab
halfway is exactly who that is for.

extract_strings.mjs now enumerates library-*.js files from the
folder instead of reading them off a hand-kept list: a text added to
a level nobody remembers would still get its recordings, instead of
silently falling back to system synthesis.

entry.title: feat(chat): add unscored, judged-live conversation practice
entry.content:
feat(chat): add unscored, judged-live conversation practice

The course had fourteen written conversations, each branch and
acceptable reply and mistake-to-stop-on authored by a person. This is
something else: an interlocutor that answers what the student actually
says. There is no single correct reply, so nothing halts the scene: the
correction lands beside the interlocutor's answer, never in place of
it.

Nothing here is scored. No card, no streak, no XP, no lesson. There is
no path from this screen into progress, which is also why the mode
needs no equivalent of clamp: no verdict to bound in the first place.

Turn history travels as the third field of the prompt and gets
translated into three dialects, not four, because OpenAI and Groq
share one. Stripped of history the request body comes out identical to
before, which doubles as a regression test: the same functions still
serve the judge, the one function the course cannot afford to lose.

Session budget is kept separate from the judge's. Sharing it would
have switched off that other function in silence, and the student
would only notice from an exercise that stops being graded, with
nothing on screen connecting the two.

A third consent, distinct and revocable: what leaves the device here
is not one sentence but the whole scene transcript, and it resets on
every turn. Accepting that one sentence gets checked is not accepting
this. The conversation lives in page memory only and never reaches the
backup file.

The interlocutor has no recordings and cannot: its lines are born
mid-conversation, not stored under data/core/, so system synthesis
reads them aloud and the screen says so.

entry.title: feat(cils): add non-scoring review of exam writing and speaking
entry.content:
feat(cils): add non-scoring review of exam writing and speaking

The exam simulator gave a real score for listening and reading and
stayed silent on the two productions. Now a model reads them and
gives two or three concrete points quoting the candidate's own
words, without grading them.

The ban on scoring moves from the prompt into CODE (cils-report.js,
on the model of LlmRules.clamp): any sentence with a fraction, a
percentage, a number next to "points", a "9 out of 12" or a verdict
word in six languages is dropped. A model that ignores the
instruction produces a shorter review, never a grade. This exam
decides someone's residence permit.

The oral test arrives in two steps: recording during the test, text
afterward, in an untimed review where the student replays it and
writes what they said. Live transcription isn't viable (audio.js:258
closes on first silence, and two microphone streams don't coexist).
The report calls it "the student's words", never a transcript. This
finally honors point 5 of ADR-009, by a different road.

The self-assessment grid is gone from the oral test: it was option G,
which ADR-009 had rejected and which still lived in the code anyway.

Two defects found by looking at the render, not by a test: the
report's two buttons printed the raw i18n keys cils.again and
cils.backToList, used in the code and defined in no language. A gate
now compares the literal keys in code and markup against the
dictionaries.

The privacy notice now states that the essay and the oral review
leave the simulator, and that the voice never does.

entry.title: feat(retention): remind the course exists without notifications
entry.content:
feat(retention): remind the course exists without notifications

The course had no way to get itself remembered: scheduled
notifications vanished from the only browser that ever had them,
and push needs a server this project deliberately doesn't have.
What's left is four things and none of them a notification:
a persistent badge, an icon counter, an install prompt, and an
.ics file run by whatever calendar the student already opened.

The counter is off by default and that's a privacy decision, not
a preference: it's the one thing the course draws outside its own
page, visible to anyone glancing at the phone.

It counts cards due within a day across both decks, vocabulary and
the error notebook. Within a day because the number is written when
the student leaves and nobody updates it while they're away, so "now"
would show zero to someone who just finished reviewing. Both decks
because the in-course counter next to "Powtórki" already sums them,
and two counters with the same name can't show two different numbers.

ics.js is a pure function because this is a format that breaks
silently and in someone else's calendar app: a stray comma or
newline doesn't damage the line, it TERMINATES it, and the limit
is 75 octets, not characters, which lands somewhere else once
accented letters are in the mix.

Every browser API used here is feature-detected before use; where
it's missing, the explanation takes the button's place, never a
dead control.

entry.title: docs(claude): generate the baseline table instead of hand-writing it
entry.content:
docs(claude): generate the baseline table instead of hand-writing it

The Baseline table in CLAUDE.md was maintained by hand and turned out
wrong more than once without anyone deciding it should change (it said
12 readings when there were 24). scripts/baseline.mjs now prints the
real numbers, so updating the table is a copy of its output, and a stale
table is a diff away from being caught. The source of truth is a
deterministic script, not memory, and a missing global exits with code 1
instead of silently printing zero.

The comment in store.js claimed merge() drops keys outside the defaults,
when it actually copies them through, which is why llmConsent and
llmOrder survive a reload despite not being in defaultState().

Plan artifacts for this work live in specs/006-input-e-produzione/.

entry.title: docs: the test and coverage figures match what the suite does today
entry.content:
docs: the test and coverage figures match what the suite does today

Every number here was read off a run made now, not off the previous
version of these files: 944 unit assertions in 40 files, 263 in Chromium,
53 mutations over seven engine files, 99.3% unit coverage, 13 979 lines of
engine. The figures they replace described the suite of an earlier release
and had drifted without anybody deciding anything.

The quality-gates section also says where the badges come from, so the next
reader knows which numbers are typed by hand (these) and which are written
by CI (the two in badges/).

entry.title: ci(badges): publish test and coverage badges for the profile page
entry.content:
ci(badges): publish test and coverage badges for the profile page

The profile README reads a shields.io endpoint badge per repository, and
this one had none: its cells carried numbers typed by hand, which describe
the suite as it was on the day somebody wrote them down.

The two figures now come out of the runs the gates already do. The three
test steps tee their output into reports/, badges.mjs reads the counts and
the coverage from there, and CI commits the result on main. No second run:
the DOM suite costs a minute and a half and a badge is not worth spending
it twice.

The unit count is read off the output of `npm test` rather than a TAP file,
because `npm test -- --test-reporter=tap` silently does nothing: node
ignores its own options after the glob. The alternative was a second npm
script repeating the pattern of the test files in a place nothing keeps in
step with this one.

An unreadable report exits 1 instead of writing a grey badge: a green build
carrying "N/A" is a failure nobody goes looking for.
